text:
**Short answer:** For one charger that handles a laptop and a phone, I'd get the **Anker 735 (Nano II 65W)**. It's $29.99 at Newegg: [buy here](https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3).

**Why the Anker 735**
- It has two USB-C ports and one USB-A. Either USB-C port gives the full 65W to a single device, which covers a MacBook Air or Dell XPS 13 (Anker's spec list: https://service.anker.com/product-description/a085g000004x2BVAAY).
- With a laptop on USB-C 1 and a phone on USB-C 2, the split is 45W + 20W. With all three ports in use, it drops to 40W / 12W / 12W.
- Anker's spec sheet lists PPS support, which matters for Samsung phones. One review (Laptopbee) says this model lacks PPS, so check this if you have a Galaxy.
- It's small (about 2.6 × 1.5 × 1.15 in), has foldable prongs, and comes with an 18-month warranty (Newegg listing).

**Alternatives**
- **UGREEN Nexode Pro 65W:** Smart Gadget Kit's top pick for travel. It's 113g, has three ports, and shows the same 45W + 20W split with two devices. It also ships with US, UK, and EU plug heads. The search results gave no direct purchase link, so look it up on Amazon or UGREEN's store. Review: https://smartgadgetkit.com/best-gan-charger/
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W, 2-pack:** $49.99 for two chargers, which is handy if you want one for home and one for your bag. It supports PPS and has a 45W + 20W split with two devices. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric is paid if you buy. That source's page only covered Baseus, so it didn't compare against Anker or UGREEN.
- **Baseus Enercore 67W:** Tom's Hardware's best 65W-range pick. It held full output in testing, ran coolest, and costs $29.99. It has a built-in retractable USB-C cable plus two more USB-C ports. Review: https://www.tomshardware.com/peripherals/usb/best-usb-chargers

**Things to know**
- If your laptop needs a full 65W, charge it alone or on the primary port. Sharing the charger with a phone cuts the laptop to 45W or less.
- None of these include a cable, so buy a 100W-rated USB-C cable if you don't have one.
- For a 14" or 16" MacBook Pro or a gaming laptop, 65W is too low. Look at a 100W charger instead.

Let me know your laptop model and phone, and I can say whether 65W is enough and which of these fits best.
